name: Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen
dates: c. 330–379 and c. 329–390 · Cappadocia and Constantinople
history: Two friends from Cappadocia, in what is now Turkey, who met as students in Athens and gave their lives to Christ and the Church. Basil, bishop of Caesarea, wrote a monastic rule still followed in the East and cared for the poor on a great scale. Gregory, a reluctant bishop and a poet, preached on the Trinity in Constantinople with such clarity that the East calls him the Theologian.
life: Basil came from a family of saints: his grandmother Macrina, his parents, his sister Macrina and his brothers Gregory of Nyssa and Peter are all honoured as saints. At Athens he formed a lifelong friendship with Gregory, who later wrote that they seemed to have one soul in two bodies. Drawn by his sister to the monastic life, Basil drew up with Gregory guidance for monks living in community. As bishop of Caesarea from 370 he stood firm against the Arian emperor Valens and built a great complex outside the city for the sick, the poor and travellers. Gregory, who longed for solitude, was made a bishop against his will. In 379 he went to Constantinople, where the Catholic faithful were a small flock, and his sermons on the Trinity turned the city. He presided for a time over the Council of 381, then withdrew to pray and write poetry.
prayerTo: Saints Basil and Gregory, friends in Christ, you studied together, prayed together and defended the faith together. Pray for all who teach and preach, that they may hand on the truth whole and clearly. Pray for me, that my friendships may lead me and others closer to God, and that I may serve Christ in the poor. Amen.
penance: Basil taught that the bread we store up belongs to the hungry. Give to a food bank today, and pray for a friend who has helped your faith.
meditation: Gregory wrote that he and Basil knew only two roads, one to the church and one to their teachers. Which of your friendships lead you towards God?
